work: Enarratio in Epistolam I B. Petri
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: ELUCIDATIO RESIDUÆ PARTIS HUJUS PRIMI CAPITULI, AB EO LOCO QUO DICITUR : ET SI PATREM INVOCATIS EUM.
1.title_en: Elucidation of the remaining part of this first chapter, from the place where it is said: And if you invoke as Father him

paras.t: Quoniam Salomone testante, timor Dei est fons vitæ, consequenter hortatur gloriosissimus apostolici chori hierarcha, sanctissimus Petrus, ut Deum filialiter timeamus. Et si, pro quia, patrem invocatis, id est, orando patrem nominatis, eum qui sine acceptione personarum judicat secundum uniuscujusque opus, id est, quemlibet judicat secundum opera sua : intelligendo per opera, etiam actus interiores, et locutiones, debitorumque actuum omissiones. Unde apud Job inducitur : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas : opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet. Et Jeremias ait : Domine Deus fortissime, cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas. Qualiter autem personarum acceptio non competat Deo, et quid sit personarum acceptio, et de peccato ipsius, dictum est supra in expositione secundi capituli epistolæ Jacobi. In timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini, id est, tempore quo in hoc sæculo subsistitis, vivite in Dei timore filiali, ne tanto patre sitis indigni, et ne in sui judicii incidatis rigorem, propter vestram ignaviam ac periculosam securitatem : ne judicem districtum aliquando sentiatis, quem nunc pium patrem contemnitis, et timere ac honorare recusatis. Qui enim sine timore est, justificari non potest. Et Christus in Evangelio jubet : Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam.
paras.en: Since, as Solomon testifies, the fear of God is a fountain of life[[Prov 14:27||]], the most glorious hierarch of the apostolic choir, most holy Peter, next exhorts us to fear God as sons. [[1:17|And if|Et si]], that is, since, [[1:17|you invoke as Father|patrem invocatis]], that is, name him Father in praying, [[1:17|him who, without respect of persons, judgeth according to every one's work|eum qui sine acceptione personarum judicat secundum uniuscujusque opus]], that is, judges each according to his works: understanding by works also interior acts, and speech, and the omission of acts that were due. Hence in Job it is said: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]: [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]]. And Jeremias says: [[Jer 32:18|O most mighty|Domine Deus fortissime]], [[Jer 32:19|whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways|cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas]]. How respect of persons does not befit God, what respect of persons is, and of its sin, has been said above in the exposition of the second chapter of the epistle of James[[Jas 2:1||]][[Jas 2:9||]]. [[1:17|converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here|In timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini]], that is, in the time in which you abide in this world, live in the filial fear of God, lest you be unworthy of so great a Father, and lest you fall into the rigour of his judgment through your sloth and perilous security: lest one day you feel as a strict judge him whom now you despise as a loving Father, and refuse to fear and honour. For he that is without fear cannot be justified[[Ecclus 1:28||]]. And Christ commands in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:28|fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam]].

paras.t: Sed instare quis potest, quia non videtur adaptatio ista Petri apostoli convenire adaptationi qua apud Malachiam loquitur Deus : Filius honorat patrem, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? et si dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus? Ex quibus verbis elicitur, quod Deo debetur timor, in quantum est dominus, et honor, in quantum est pater. Quomodo ergo nunc ait Apostolus, Si patrem invocatis Deum, in timore conversamini? Videtur enim debuisse dixisse, Si dominum invocatis, etc. — Et respondendum, quod Deo debetur timor castus, sanctus et filialis, in quantum est pater, quia hic timor ex magnitudine oritur caritatis. Timor vero servilis aut initialis impenditur Deo, ut domino. Est autem timor filialis, quo vitatur malum culpæ ne Deus pater offendatur aut inhonoretur. Sicque timor filialis realiter est fuga seu abominatio culpæ. De quo in Ecclesiastico multa scribuntur, videlicet : Timor Domini super omnia se superposuit. Beatus cui datum est habere timorem Dei. Timor Domini sicut paradisus benedictionis. Est autem timor Dei omni Christiano præcipue necessarius, quia præservat a vitiis, custodit in bonis, et sollicitum facit timentem, ne cadat in laqueos inimici. Iterum, semper coram Deo solliciti esse debemus ac pavidi, quia nescimus an digni simus amore vel odio, hoc est, an simus in caritate et gratia, an non : et rursus, quoniam ignoramus quid finaliter erit nobis, an scilicet sempiterna damnatio, an salus perpetua; et quia ad omne malum sumus tam proni, atque in laqueorum medio ambulamus.
paras.en: But someone may object that this adaptation of the apostle Peter does not seem to agree with that by which God speaks in Malachias: [[Mal 1:6|The son honoureth the father, and the servant his master: if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear|Filius honorat patrem, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? et si dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus?]]? From these words it is drawn that fear is owed to God inasmuch as he is Lord, and honour inasmuch as he is Father. How then does the Apostle now say: If you invoke God as Father, converse in fear? He seems to have ought to say: If you invoke him as Lord, etc. — And it must be answered that chaste, holy and filial fear is owed to God inasmuch as he is Father, for this fear arises from the greatness of charity. But servile or initial fear [that is, the fear of punishment, and the beginner's fear mixed of love and dread of punishment] is paid to God as Lord. Filial fear is that by which the evil of fault is shunned lest God the Father be offended or dishonoured. And thus filial fear is really a flight from, or abhorrence of, fault. Of it much is written in Ecclesiasticus, namely: [[Ecclus 25:14|The fear of God hath set itself above all things|Timor Domini super omnia se superposuit]]. [[Ecclus 25:15|Blessed is the man, to whom it is given to have the fear of God|Beatus cui datum est habere timorem Dei]]. [[Ecclus 40:28|The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing|Timor Domini sicut paradisus benedictionis]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xi, 28; the words stand at Ecclus 40:28]. Now the fear of God is especially necessary to every Christian, for it preserves from vices, keeps in good things, and makes him who fears watchful lest he fall into the snares of the enemy. Again, we ought always to be watchful and trembling before God, for we know not whether we be worthy of love or hatred[[Eccles 9:1||]], that is, whether we be in charity and grace or not; and again because we know not what will finally be ours, whether everlasting damnation or perpetual salvation; and because we are so prone to every evil, and walk in the midst of snares.

paras.t: Præterea, ad conversandum tam timorate ac virtuose nos debet inducere, quod Unigenitus Dei, verus Deus, tanta pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit ac pertulit. Ideo subditur : Scientes per fidem, non per naturalem rationem : de qua scientia dixit Job, Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum ; Martha quoque : Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die ; quod non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis, id est originalis infectionis seu vitiosæ informationis : quia parentes istorum quibus hæc scripta sunt, filios suos pessime docuerunt, ut scilicet idola colerent, quantum ad eos qui ex gentilibus nati erant. Sacerdotes quoque et Scribæ Judæorum, tradiderunt filiis suis ac subditis quædam divinæ legi contraria : quibus in Evangelio loquitur Christus, Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditionem vestram.
paras.en: Moreover, what ought to lead us to live so fearfully and virtuously is that the Only-begotten of God, true God, took on, did and endured such great things for our salvation. Therefore it is added: [[1:18|Knowing|Scientes]], by faith, not by natural reason; of which knowledge Job said: [[Job 19:25|I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]]; and Martha too: [[John 11:24|I know that he shall rise again, in the resurrection at the last day|Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die]]; [[1:18|that you were not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver, from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers|quod non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis]], that is, of original infection, or of vicious instruction: for the parents of those to whom this was written taught their sons most wickedly, namely to worship idols, as regards those born of the Gentiles. The priests and Scribes of the Jews also handed down to their sons and subjects certain things contrary to the divine law; to whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 15:6|you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition|Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditionem vestram]].

paras.t: Sed pretioso sanguine, quasi agni incontaminati et immaculati. Jesu Christi, id est passione et morte Filii Dei, qui est quasi agnus, quoniam innocentissimo agno assimilatur. De quo ait Joannes Baptista : Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Qui et per Jeremiam contestatur : Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam. Estque quasi agnus incontaminatus et immaculatus, propter immunitatem suam ab omni peccato, tam originali quam personali, tam mortali quam veniali. Christus quippe, quamvis pro originalis peccati deletione specialiter passus dicatur, sua tamen passione sanctissima pro cunctis totius humani generis peccatis, quantum in ipso est, satisfecit, juxta illud Isaiæ : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Propter quod angelus dixit ad Joseph : Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum : ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. —
paras.en: [[1:19|But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unspotted and undefiled|Sed pretioso sanguine, quasi agni incontaminati et immaculati]], of Jesus Christ, that is, by the passion and death of the Son of God, who is as a lamb, since he is likened to a most innocent lamb. Of whom John the Baptist says: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi]]. Who also testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]. And he is as a lamb unspotted and undefiled because of his freedom from all sin, original as well as personal, mortal as well as venial. For Christ, though he is said to have suffered especially for the blotting out of original sin, yet by his most holy passion made satisfaction, as far as lay in him, for all the sins of the whole human race, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. Wherefore the angel said to Joseph: [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus. For he shall save his people from their sins|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum : ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]. —

paras.t: Christi, inquam, præcogniti quidem ante constitutionem mundi, id est ab æterno ad hoc præordinati ac prævisi a Deo Patre, secundum naturam assumptam, ut per eum redimeretur genus humanum. Deus namque ab æterno decrevit per Christi passionem redimere mundum. Manifestati autem in novissimis temporibus propter vos, id est, propter vestram salutem, Christus in ultima mundi ætate per incarnationis mysterium apparuit in hoc mundo, juxta illud Baruch : Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. Hoc est quod ait Joannes : Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Hinc ad Ephesios loquitur Paulus, dicendo : Deus elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem, in quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ejus. De his demum diebus novissimis loquitur Paulus : Nos sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt.
paras.en: Of Christ, I say, [[1:20|Foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world|præcogniti quidem ante constitutionem mundi]], that is, from eternity foreordained and foreseen for this by God the Father, according to the nature assumed, that through him mankind should be redeemed. For God decreed from eternity to redeem the world by the passion of Christ. [[1:20|but manifested in the last times for you|Manifestati autem in novissimis temporibus propter vos]], that is, for your salvation, Christ appeared in this world in the last age of the world through the mystery of the Incarnation, according to that of Baruch: [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]. This is what John says: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. Hence Paul speaks to the Ephesians, saying: [[Eph 1:4|he chose us in him before the foundation of the world|elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem]], [[Eph 1:7|In whom we have redemption through his blood|in quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ejus]]. Of these last days, finally, Paul speaks: [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]].

paras.t: Qui per ipsum fideles estis in Deo, id est, virtute et merito passionis Christi, gratiam conversionis ac fidei consecuti estis a Deo, et hucusque fideles mansistis in eo. Meritum etenim Christi in sacramento Baptismi ac Pœnitentiæ applicatur hominibus : et quidquid virtutis et gratiæ eis confertur a Domino, per Christum et ejus passionem ac meritum ipsis donatur, in quantum per Christi mysteria Deus proposuit sibi reconciliare atque salvare genus humanum. Propter quod ad Ephesios habetur : Deus prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum in laudem gloriæ gratiæ suæ, in qua gratificavit nos in dilecto Filio suo. Vel, Per ipsum fideles estis in Deo, quoniam Christus suos misit discipulos ad aliorum conversionem ubique, et per Apostolos dedit hominibus legem salutis, quemadmodum apud Isaiam ait : Lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet. Idcirco ait Apostolus : In Christo, qui eratis longe, facti estis prope.
paras.en: [[1:21|Who through him are faithful in God|Qui per ipsum fideles estis in Deo]], that is, by the power and merit of Christ's passion you have obtained from God the grace of conversion and of faith, and have hitherto remained faithful in him. For the merit of Christ is applied to men in the sacrament of Baptism and of Penance; and whatever virtue and grace is conferred on them by the Lord is given them through Christ and his passion and merit, inasmuch as God purposed to reconcile mankind to himself and save it through the mysteries of Christ. Wherefore it is said to the Ephesians: [[Eph 1:5|predestinated us unto the adoption of children through Jesus Christ|prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum]] [[Eph 1:6|Unto the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he hath graced us, in his beloved son|in laudem gloriæ gratiæ suæ, in qua gratificavit nos in dilecto Filio suo]]. Or: Through him you are faithful in God, because Christ sent his disciples everywhere for the conversion of others, and through the Apostles gave men the law of salvation, as he says in Isaias: [[Is 51:4|a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest to be a light of the nations|Lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet]]. Therefore the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:13|in Christ Jesus, you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh|In Christo, qui eratis longe, facti estis prope]].

paras.t: Qui suscitavit eum a mortuis tertia die. Quæ suscitatio toti superbenedictæ Trinitati, cujus opera ad extra sunt indivisa, adscribitur. Potest tamen Patri appropriari, quia divina virtute effecta est : virtus autem seu potentia Patri appropriatur. Imo Christus, secundum quod est Deus, suscitavit se ipsum ut homo est. Propter quod dixit : Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Et dedit ei gloriam sempiternam, id est perpetuam corporis glorificationem, accidentaleque præmium, et judiciariam potestatem, in resurrectione, ascensione, etc. Nam in beatifica Dei visione, anima Christi fuit, ab exordio suæ creationis et unionis cum Verbo, perfecta. Hinc Christus passione sua instante, oravit illud Joannis : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Et ad Hebræos habetur : Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum. In Isaia quoque legitur : Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur. Ut fides vestra et spes esset in Domino, id est, firmiter crederetis in Deum, et speraretis in eo. Ex hoc enim quod Deus Christum ita glorificavit per resuscitationem, ascensionem, et Sancti Spiritus missionem, inducti sunt homines ad christianæ fidei ac spei susceptionem, credentes et sperantes se tandem merito Christi resuscitandos et plene glorificandos.
paras.en: [[1:21|who raised him up from the dead|qui suscitavit eum a mortuis]] on the third day. This raising is ascribed to the whole superblessed Trinity, whose works outwardly are undivided. Yet it can be appropriated to the Father, since it was wrought by divine power, and power or might is appropriated to the Father [that is, attributed to one Person by a fitting likeness, though common to all three]. Nay, Christ, as he is God, raised up himself as he is man. Wherefore he said: [[John 2:19|Destroy this temple; and in three days I will raise it up|Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud]]. [[1:21|and hath given him glory|Et dedit ei gloriam]] everlasting, that is, the perpetual glorification of the body, and accidental reward, and judiciary power, in the resurrection, ascension, etc. For in the beatific vision of God the soul of Christ was perfect from the beginning of its creation and union with the Word. Hence Christ, as his passion drew near, prayed that prayer in John: [[John 17:1|said: the hour is come. Glorify thy Son, that thy Son|Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. And it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:9|we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour|Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum]]. In Isaias too we read: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]]. [[1:21|that your faith and hope might be in God|Ut fides vestra et spes esset in Domino]], that is, that you might firmly believe in God and hope in him. For because God so glorified Christ by the resurrection, ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, men were led to receive the Christian faith and hope, believing and hoping that by the merit of Christ they would at last be raised up and fully glorified.

paras.t: Animas vestras castificantes, id est, cœlesti Sponso castas et puras exhibentes, in obedientia caritatis, id est obediendo divinis præceptis ex caritate, sine qua nulla est actio meritoria, Deoque grata. Omnis siquidem actus meritorius, est a caritate elicitive, ut actus qui immediate et directe procedunt ex caritate; aut imperative, ut actus aliarum virtutum quibus præcipit caritas. In fraternitatis amore, id est etiam in proximorum spirituali dilectione, sine qua nemo potest salvari. Ideo subditur : simplici ex corde, omni duplicitate et fictione exclusa, invicem diligite attentius, id est valde attente, quum dicat Salvator : In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem. Atque ut asserit Paulus : Qui diligit proximum, legem implevit. Porro de cordis simplicitate et duplicitate, dicta sunt multa super Canonicam Jacobi.
paras.en: [[1:22|Purifying your souls|Animas vestras castificantes]], that is, presenting them chaste and pure to the heavenly Bridegroom, [[1:22|in the obedience of charity|in obedientia caritatis]], that is, obeying the divine commandments out of charity, without which no action is meritorious and pleasing to God[[1 Cor 13:1||]]. For every meritorious act is from charity either elicitively, as the acts which proceed immediately and directly from charity, or imperatively, as the acts of the other virtues which charity commands [the scholastic distinction between acts produced by a virtue itself and acts of other virtues which it directs]. [[1:22|with a brotherly love|In fraternitatis amore]], that is, also in the spiritual love of our neighbours, without which no one can be saved. Therefore it is added: [[1:22|from a sincere heart|simplici ex corde]], all doubleness and pretence excluded, [[1:22|love one another earnestly|invicem diligite attentius]], that is, very attentively, since the Saviour says: [[John 13:35|By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another|In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]]. And as Paul asserts: [[Rom 13:8|he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law|Qui diligit proximum, legem implevit]]. Further, much was said of simplicity and doubleness of heart on the Canonical Epistle of James[[Jas 1:8||]].

paras.t: Omnis autem anima rationalis, aut est sponsa Dei per fidem ac caritatem, aut certe adultera diaboli per infidelitatem, seu quamcumque culpam mortalem. Ideo animas nostras castificare debemus modo prætacto, et omni virtute ornare, sanctis actibus decorare, incessabiliter, fructuose, timorate ac fervide conversari : præsertim quoniam tanti æstimavit nos Dominus Deus noster, quod propter nostram recuperandam salutem, nostram in unitate personæ assumpsit naturam, et in ea pro nobis tot et tanta fecit ac passus est. Nonne ex dignitate legati, magnitudo causæ pensatur? Quum ergo Unigenitum suum miserit Deus Pater legatum ad pacificandum nos sibi, quis magnitudinem causæ quam cum Deo habemus, excellentiamque beatitudinis ad quam sumus creati, concipere valeat aut effari? Hinc et aliam causam ob quam timorate vivere debeamus, dignissimus apostolici chori vertex subjungit.
paras.en: Every rational soul is either the bride of God through faith and charity, or else the adulteress of the devil through unbelief or any mortal fault. Therefore we must purify our souls in the manner touched on, adorn them with every virtue, beautify them with holy acts, and live unceasingly, fruitfully, fearfully and fervently: above all since the Lord our God esteemed us so highly that, to recover our salvation, he assumed our nature in the unity of his person, and in it did and suffered so many and so great things for us. Is not the greatness of a cause weighed by the dignity of the envoy? Since then God the Father sent his Only-begotten as envoy to make our peace with him, who can conceive or utter the greatness of the cause we have with God, and the excellence of the beatitude for which we were created? Hence the most worthy head of the apostolic choir adds another reason why we ought to live in fear.

paras.t: Renati non ex semine corruptibili, id est, Deum timere, invicemque attentius amare debetis, quia renati estis seu spiritualiter generati per emundationem a culpa, et susceptionem gratiæ ac virtutum, non ex materiali impuroque semine, sed incorruptibili, id est virtute cœlesti in sacramento Baptismatis operante, seu gratia spirituali et gratum faciente, quæ confert homini esse spirituale, supernaturale, deiforme, idoneum ad promerendum. per verbum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum, id est per Christum, de quo Joannes ait : Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Nam Christus est qui principaliter interiusque baptizat, purgat, regenerat. Ipse quoque Baptismum instituit, et omnibus dari præcepit ; et ipse est Verbum increatum, æternum, unigenitum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum, videlicet Patris æterni, quemadmodum Petrus disseruit : Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi. Vel per verbum Dei vivi, intelligit formam verborum sacramentalium operantium in Baptismo, per quæ dispositive et suo modo causaliter fit regeneratio spiritualis : quoniam accedente verbo ad elementum, fit sacramentum. Unde et Paulus testatur, quod Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ. De hac regeneratione dicta sunt plura super illud Jacobi, Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis. Unde Joannes ait : Dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, his qui credunt in nomine ejus, qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.
paras.en: [[1:23|Being born again, not of corruptible seed|Renati non ex semine corruptibili]]: that is, you ought to fear God and love one another more earnestly, because you are born again, or spiritually begotten, through cleansing from fault and the receiving of grace and the virtues, not of material and impure seed, [[1:23|but incorruptible|sed incorruptibili]], that is, by the heavenly power working in the sacrament of Baptism, or by spiritual and sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], which gives man a spiritual, supernatural, godlike being, fit for meriting. [[1:23|by the word of God who liveth and remaineth for ever|per verbum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum]], that is, through Christ, of whom John says: [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|Omnia per ipsum facta sunt]]. For it is Christ who principally and inwardly baptizes, cleanses, regenerates. He also instituted Baptism and commanded it to be given to all; and he is the uncreated, eternal Word, the only-begotten of the living God who remains for ever, namely of the eternal Father, as Peter declared: [[Matt 16:16|Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God|Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi]]. Or by the word of the living God he means the form of the sacramental words working in Baptism, through which spiritual regeneration takes place dispositively and in its own way causally: for when the word is joined to the element, the sacrament is made. Hence Paul too testifies that [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam]], [[Eph 5:26|cleansing it by the laver of water in the word of life|mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ]]. Of this regeneration much was said on that of James: [[Jas 1:18|of his own will hath he begotten us by the word of truth|Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis]]. Hence John says: [[John 1:12|he gave them power to be made the sons of God, to them that believe in his name|Dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, his qui credunt in nomine ejus]], [[John 1:13|Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God|qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt]].

paras.t: Quia omnis caro fœnum. Tanquam dicat : Regeneratio spiritualis, ex carnali et corruptibili semine esse nequit : quoniam caro carnaleve semen, fœno assimilatur, idcirco ad spirituale et supernaturale esse non potest perducere, nec talis generationis semen exsistere. Unde ait Salvator : Quod natum est ex carne, caro est; et quod natum est ex spiritu, spiritus est. Et omnis gloria ejus, id est viror, vigor, voluptasque carnis, quasi flos fœni, id est, cito pertransit et deficit, sicut flos graminis. Exaruit fœnum, id est, gramen, postquam viruerit et excreverit, mox arescit, et flos ejus decidit. Sic caro in pueritia habet virorem, in adolescentia decorem, in juventute robur et florem, in senectute desiccationem, in morte corruptionem.
paras.en: [[1:24|For all flesh is as grass|Quia omnis caro fœnum]]. As though he said: Spiritual regeneration cannot come from carnal and corruptible seed; for flesh, or carnal seed, is likened to grass[[Is 40:6||]][[Ecclus 14:18||]], and therefore cannot bring one to spiritual and supernatural being, nor be the seed of such a generation. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 3:6|That which is born of the flesh is flesh: and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit|quod natum est ex spiritu, spiritus est]]. [[1:24|and all the glory thereof|Et omnis gloria ejus]], that is, the freshness, vigour and pleasure of the flesh, [[1:24|as the flower of grass|quasi flos fœni]], that is, quickly passes away and fails, like the flower of the grass. [[1:24|The grass is withered|Exaruit fœnum]], that is, the grass, after it has grown green and tall, soon dries up, [[1:24|and the flower thereof is fallen away|et flos ejus decidit]]. So the flesh has in childhood freshness, in youth comeliness, in manhood strength and bloom, in old age drying up, in death corruption.

paras.t: Verbum autem Domini manet in æternum. Quod primo verum est de Verbo increato Patris æterni. De quo scriptum est : In principio erat Verbum. De quo Damascenus intelligit illud in Psalmo, In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum permanet in cœlo. Secundo, verificatur de verbo creato, id est divinæ virtutis præcepto, effectu seu lege, qua cuncta subsistunt. De quo verbo cantatur : Ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, quæ faciunt verbum ejus ; et rursus, Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit. Tertio, de verbo sacræ Scripturæ, quod dicitur non transire, sed in æternum manere. Nam inviolabilis atque perpetua est veritas Scripturarum, quamvis verba vocalia sonando transeant, ac desinant esse, utpote de numero successivorum, quibus idem est esse et fieri. Ideo loquitur Christus : Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt. Quarto, de verbo sacramentali, quod manet in suo effectu. Nam character qui in Baptismo imprimitur, indelebilis perhibetur. Et gratia quæ ibi infunditur, ex se non habet ut corrumpatur, quamvis per accidens desinat esse in transgressore : quæ etiam gratia arrha vitæ æternæ vocatur. — Denique locus hic ex Isaia sumptus est, ubi habetur : Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri, etc.
paras.en: [[1:25|But the word of the Lord endureth for ever|Verbum autem Domini manet in æternum]]. This is true first of the uncreated Word of the eternal Father, of whom it is written: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. Of whom Damascene understands that in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:89|For ever, O Lord, thy word standeth firm in heaven|In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum permanet in cœlo]]. Secondly, it is verified of the created word, that is, the command, effect or law of the divine power by which all things subsist. Of which word it is sung: [[Ps 148:8|Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds, which fulfil his word|Ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, quæ faciunt verbum ejus]]; and again: [[Ps 148:6|he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away|Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit]]. Thirdly, of the word of Holy Scripture, which is said not to pass but to remain for ever. For the truth of the Scriptures is inviolable and perpetual, though the spoken words pass in the sounding and cease to be, being of the number of successive things, for which to be and to come to be are the same. Therefore Christ says: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away|Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt]]. Fourthly, of the sacramental word, which remains in its effect. For the character imprinted in Baptism is held to be indelible. And the grace infused there has not of itself that it should be corrupted, though accidentally it ceases to be in the transgressor; which grace is also called the pledge of eternal life. — Lastly, this passage is taken from Isaias, where we have: [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri]], etc.[[Is 40:8||]]

paras.t: Hoc autem est verbum quod evangelizatum est in vobis, id est, inter vos prædicatum per Christi Apostolos ceterosque discipulos : qui, Paulo testante, non prædicaverunt se ipsos, sed Jesum Christum, qui est Verbum æternum, et ejus doctrinam, præcepta ac sacramenta.
paras.en: [[1:25|And this is the word which by the gospel hath been preached unto you|Hoc autem est verbum quod evangelizatum est in vobis]], that is, preached among you by the Apostles of Christ and his other disciples, who, as Paul testifies, [[2 Cor 4:5|preach not ourselves, but Jesus Christ|non prædicaverunt se ipsos, sed Jesum Christum]], who is the eternal Word, and his doctrine, commandments and sacraments.

3.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS HUJUS CAPITULI TERTII, AB EO LOCO: ET QUIS EST QUI VOBIS NOCEAT?
3.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this third chapter, from the place: And who is he that can hurt you?

paras.t: ABUNDAVIT in primitiva Ecclesia Christianorum persecutio copiosa, ferox, assidua. Idcirco conversi ad fidem, indigebant confortatione et informatione ad patientiam. Et hoc nunc agit Apostolorum dignissimus vertex. Et quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis? Tanquam dicat: Nullus vobis potest nocere, si æmulatores, hoc est amatores seu imitatores, estis boni, hoc est Dei seu Christi essentialiter boni; vel, Boni, id est virtutis. Nam qui hujusmodi boni est æmulator, non dejicitur per adversa, sed Deo firmiter est inhærens. Idcirco tribulatio cooperatur ei in meritorum augmentum; et si lædatur in corpore, si spolietur substantia, si diffametur, non ei hæc nocent, sed mirabiliter prosunt, si ea æquanimiter ferat, quemadmodum ægro non nocet amara potio, sectio sive adustio. Ideo dictum est: Nulla nocebit adversitas, si nulla dominetur iniquitas. Eis vero qui inferunt ista justis, maxime nocet horum illatio, quum peccent mortaliter. Uniuscujusque siquidem malum in proprium redundat auctorem. Et cui hæc nocent, ex propria impatientia, ira, seu alia culpa nocent. Ideo in Ecclesiaste dicitur: Qui fodit foveam, incidet in eam; et qui dissipat sepem, mordebit eum coluber.
paras.en: In the primitive Church the persecution of Christians abounded, plentiful, fierce and unceasing. Therefore those converted to the faith needed strengthening and instruction in patience. And this the most worthy head of the Apostles now does. [[3:13|And who is he that can hurt you, if you be zealous of good?|Et quis est qui vobis noceat, si boni æmulatores fueritis?]] As if he said: No one can hurt you, if you are zealous, that is, lovers or imitators, of the good, that is, of God or Christ, who is essentially good; or, *of good*, that is, of virtue. For he who is zealous of such good is not cast down by adversity, but cleaves firmly to God. Therefore tribulation works together for him unto the increase of merits; and if he be hurt in body, if he be stripped of his substance, if he be defamed, these things do not hurt him but wonderfully profit him, if he bear them with equanimity, just as a bitter draught, cutting or cautery does not hurt a sick man. Hence it has been said: No adversity shall hurt, if no iniquity have dominion. But to those who inflict these things on the just, the inflicting of them does the greatest hurt, since they sin mortally. For each man's evil rebounds upon its own author. And those whom these things hurt, they hurt through their own impatience, anger or other fault. Therefore it is said in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 10:8|He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him|Qui fodit foveam, incidet in eam; et qui dissipat sepem, mordebit eum coluber]].

paras.t: Sed his objici potest, quoniam, ut videtur, impiissimi hæresiarchæ valde nocuerunt multis bonis Catholicis, quorum fidem pestiferis persuasionibus everterunt. Nonne sacrilegus et damnatissimus Arius totum pene orbem infecit? Unde et Beda hic ait: Constat plurimos boni æmulatores, læsos esse ab aliis, dum in veritatis, quam diligunt, cognitione male instructi sunt. Quantos enim in Deum catholice credere et recte in Ecclesia vivere cupientes, Arii vesania, quantos Sabellii aliorumque hæreticorum nequitia nescientes seduxit? Lege Joannis Chrysostomi librum quem scripsit de eo, videlicet, Neminem posse lædi ab alio, nisi a semetipso. Hæc Beda. Verum de isto longa posset disputatio introduci. Sed brevitati studendum est, et breviter respondendum, quod sicut diabolus tentando inclinat, non compellit, homines ad peccata, ipsi vero libere consentiendo tentanti, se ipsos præcipitant: sic hæresiarchæ potuerunt inclinare, non cogere, ad errores; nec persecutores, absolute loquendo, compulerunt fideles ad sacrificandum, sed qui sacrificaverunt ex pœnis inducti, ex propria infirmitate et imperfectione cesserunt et perierunt. Hinc subditur:
paras.en: But against this it may be objected that, as it seems, the most impious heresiarchs greatly hurt many good Catholics, whose faith they overthrew by pestilent persuasions. Did not the sacrilegious and most damned Arius infect almost the whole world? Hence Bede too says here: It is certain that very many zealous of good have been hurt by others, while they were badly instructed in the knowledge of the truth which they love. For how many who desired to believe in God in the Catholic way and to live rightly in the Church did the madness of Arius, how many did the wickedness of Sabellius and other heretics seduce unawares? Read the book of John Chrysostom which he wrote on this, namely, That no one can be hurt by another, except by himself. Thus Bede. Truly a long disputation could be brought in on this. But brevity must be studied, and the brief answer is that, just as the devil by tempting inclines men to sin but does not compel them, while they, freely consenting to the tempter, cast themselves headlong: so the heresiarchs could incline men to errors, not force them; nor did the persecutors, speaking absolutely, compel the faithful to sacrifice, but those who sacrificed, induced by punishments, gave way and perished through their own weakness and imperfection. Hence it is added:

paras.t: Sed et si quid patimini propter justitiam, beati estis nunc in merito et spe, beati futuri in præmio et re: sicut ait Salvator, Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum. Et rursus, loquens diffusius, et justos plenissime recreans ac consolans, ait ibidem: Beati estis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me; gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Patiendo namque æquanimiter aspera propter justitiam, purgamur a culpis, implemur potioribus gratiæ donis, Christo assimilamur, a futuris eripimur pœnis, propinquamus ad regnum, et gloriæ promeremur augmentum. Denique, qui correptionem et correctionem pro suis peccatis gratanter suscipiunt, ut in vita præsenti purgentur ac Deo complaceant, quamvis pro suis patiantur demeritis, tamen aliquo modo, puta finaliter, propter justitiam pati dicuntur, et reputatur eis hoc ipsum ad meritum, suntque beati. Miseri vero sunt, et miseri vehementer, qui corripi ac corrigi dedignantur.
paras.en: [[3:14|But if also you suffer any thing for justice' sake, blessed are ye|Sed et si quid patimini propter justitiam, beati]] now in merit and hope, to be blessed hereafter in reward and in reality: as the Saviour says, [[Matt 5:10|Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]]. And again, speaking more at length, and most fully refreshing and consoling the just, he says in the same place: [[Matt 5:11|Blessed are ye when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and speak all that is evil against you, untruly, for my sake|Beati estis quum maledixerint vobis homines, et persecuti vos fuerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos, mentientes, propter me]]; [[Matt 5:12|Be glad and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]] [Denis reads “rejoice in that hour”]. For by suffering harsh things with equanimity for justice' sake, we are purged of faults, filled with greater gifts of grace, made like to Christ, delivered from future punishments; we draw near to the kingdom and merit an increase of glory. Finally, those who gladly accept reproof and correction for their sins, that they may be purged in the present life and please God, although they suffer for their own demerits, are yet in some manner, namely as to their end [that is, in the purpose for which they accept it], said to suffer for justice' sake; and this very thing is reckoned to them for merit, and they are blessed. But wretched, and exceedingly wretched, are those who disdain to be reproved and corrected.

paras.t: Timorem autem, id est causam timoris, videlicet crudelitatem et persecutionem, eorum qui adversa infligunt, ne timueritis, immoderato timore a virtutum constantia retrahente. Ideo subditur: ut non conturbemini, id est, ne ordinationem rationis tranquillitatemque mentis perdatis, et ita aliorum pravitate vincamini. Hinc jubet Salvator: Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt. Et in Proverbiis habetur: Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit; et in Isaia, Quis tu, ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit? Verumtamen timor adversitatum et mortis, naturalis dumtaxat, excusatur a culpa, quum et Christus timuerit mortem ex prævio rationis judicio. Aliqui vero timent se formidaturos tribulatione instante: qui quod evadere cupiunt, ante tempus assumunt. Quibus consulitur ut Dominum deprecentur, quatenus eos ab omni inordinato expurget pavore, cum Psalmista orantes, A timore inimici eripe animam meam: non ut me non occidat inimicus, sed ut non timeam occidentem inimicum. Considerent etiam quam salubre sit pati adversa, quamque proficuum, et quam brevis sit omnis tribulatio vitæ præsentis, et quanta sustinuerunt Christus et Sancti. Ex quorum omnium intuitione constantes ac fortes, imo et læti sint in tribulationibus et tormentis.
paras.en: [[3:14|And be not afraid of their fear|Timorem autem eorum ne timueritis]]: *their fear*, that is, the cause of fear, namely the cruelty and persecution of those who inflict adversities; be not afraid with an immoderate fear that draws you back from constancy in the virtues. Therefore he adds: [[3:14|and be not troubled|ut non conturbemini]], that is, lest you lose the ordering of reason and tranquillity of mind, and so be overcome by the depravity of others. Hence the Saviour commands: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt]]. And in Proverbs we have: [[Prov 28:1|the just, bold as a lion, shall be without dread|Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|Quis tu, ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit?]]? Nevertheless fear of adversities and of death, when it is merely natural, is excused from fault, since Christ too feared death with the prior judgment of reason[[Matt 26:38||]]. But some fear that they will be terrified when tribulation comes: these take up beforehand what they wish to escape. They are counselled to beseech the Lord to purge them of all inordinate dread, praying with the Psalmist: [[Ps 63:2|deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy|A timore inimici eripe animam meam]]: not that the enemy may not kill me, but that I may not fear the enemy who kills. Let them consider also how wholesome it is to suffer adversity, and how profitable, and how brief is all the tribulation of the present life, and how much Christ and the Saints endured. From the contemplation of all these let them be constant and strong, nay even joyful, in tribulations and torments.

paras.t: Dominum autem Christum sanctificate, id est, magnifice honorate, firmiterque tenete, et sanctum esse sentite, in cordibus vestris, videlicet in intellectu et voluntate, eum sinceriter contemplando, fervide diligendo, et totis viribus honorando. Juxta hunc sensum oramus assidue: Pater noster, qui es in cœlis, sanctificetur nomen tuum. Et Propheta hortatur: Magnificate Dominum mecum. Per Ezechielem quoque Dominus fatur: Quum sanctificatus fuero in vobis. Et Isaias ait: Dominum exercituum sanctificate.
paras.en: [[3:15|But sanctify the Lord Christ|Dominum autem Christum sanctificate]], that is, honour him magnificently, hold him firmly, and acknowledge him to be holy, [[3:15|in your hearts|in cordibus vestris]], namely in understanding and will, by contemplating him sincerely, loving him fervently, and honouring him with all your strength. In this sense we pray continually: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name|Pater noster, qui es in cœlis, sanctificetur nomen tuum]]. And the Prophet exhorts: [[Ps 33:4|O magnify the Lord with me|Magnificate Dominum mecum]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxiii, 3; in the Vulgate numbering the words are at 33:4]. Through Ezechiel too the Lord speaks: [[Ezech 36:23|when I shall be sanctified in you|Quum sanctificatus fuero in vobis]]. And Isaias says: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord of hosts|Dominum exercituum sanctificate]].

paras.t: Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est, fide et spe, id est, tam instructi et sapientes in evangelica lege sitis, ut jugiter prompti sitis ad dandam rationabilem responsionem et causam universis a vobis quærentibus rationes fidei vestræ ac spei: cur scilicet tam incomprehensibilia credatis, tamque supernaturalem beatitudinem, et secreta ac invisibilia bona adipisci speretis.
paras.en: [[3:15|being ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you|Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est]], [Denis's text reads “faith and hope”] that is, be so instructed and wise in the law of the Gospel that you are continually ready to give a reasonable answer and ground to all who ask of you the reasons of your faith and hope: namely why you believe things so incomprehensible, and hope to obtain so supernatural a beatitude and goods so secret and invisible.

paras.t: Potest autem quis rationem fidei ac spei interrogare a Christiano dupliciter: primo, fideliter; secundo, infideliter. Qui fideliter quærit, caritative informandus est, et potest faciliter contentari. Qui vero infideliter sciscitatur, non ita faciliter contentatur; sed opponit et arguit quousque vincatur. Utrisque tamen eædem rationes fidei ac spei sunt assignandæ, quod scilicet ita credimus et speramus: quoniam Deus altissimus, omnipotens, verax, qui nec fallere potest nec falli, huic nostræ fidei et spei testimonium perhibuit, primo per Christum, deinde per sanctos Apostolos ceterosque Christi discipulos et viros sanctos, imo per utriusque sexus personas innumerabiles, usque in præsens, per innumera et præclara miracula soli omnipotentiæ suæ possibilia: quæ partim in Scripturis canonicis sunt descripta, partim in chronicis, aliisque historiis et legendis authenticis. Secundo, quoniam quidquid de Christo credimus et speramus in evangelicæ legis Scripturis, in veteris Testamenti Scripturis per Moysen et beatos Prophetas copiose legimus prophetatum. Tertio, quia lex Christi, est lex totius sanctitatis et honestatis ac perfectionis. Quarto, per finalem istam Judæorum relictionem probamus Christum venisse. Quinto, ostenditur veritas fidei per hoc, quod quanto adversarii et tyranni atrocius nitebantur fidem christianam prorsus exstinguere, tanto plus crevit atque invaluit. Ex quibus omnibus, multisque aliis rationibus, sufficienter et certe probatur, quod fidei nostræ ac spei Deus sit auctor ac testis: quamvis per ea fidei veritates supernaturales ita probari non queant ut comprehendantur per rationem, certitudinemque evidentiæ habeant.
paras.en: Now a man may ask a Christian the reason of his faith and hope in two ways: first, faithfully; second, unfaithfully. He who asks faithfully is to be instructed charitably, and can easily be satisfied. But he who inquires unfaithfully is not so easily satisfied, but objects and argues until he is overcome. To both, however, the same reasons of faith and hope are to be given, namely why we so believe and hope: first, because the most high God, almighty and true, who can neither deceive nor be deceived, has borne witness to this our faith and hope, first through Christ, then through the holy Apostles and the other disciples of Christ and holy men, nay through innumerable persons of either sex down to the present, by countless and glorious miracles possible to his omnipotence alone: which are recorded partly in the canonical Scriptures, partly in chronicles and other authentic histories and legends. Second, because whatever we believe and hope concerning Christ in the Scriptures of the Gospel law, we read abundantly prophesied in the Scriptures of the Old Testament through Moses and the blessed Prophets. Third, because the law of Christ is a law of all holiness, uprightness and perfection. Fourth, by this final abandonment of the Jews we prove that Christ has come. Fifth, the truth of the faith is shown by this, that the more fiercely adversaries and tyrants strove utterly to extinguish the Christian faith, the more it grew and prevailed. From all these and many other reasons it is sufficiently and certainly proved that God is the author and witness of our faith and hope: although by them the supernatural truths of faith cannot be so proved as to be comprehended by reason and to have the certitude of evidence.

paras.t: Verumtamen, fidem contra adversariorum disputationem defendere, et eam diversis argumentationibus rationabiliter persuadere ac declarare, non est omnium, sed specialiter eruditorum. Nec est præceptum ut unusquisque fidelis paratus sit ad satisfaciendum quærentibus rationem fidei ac spei, quum multi sint idiotæ et penitus simplices; sed istud est magis consilium. Prælati tamen et superiores atque doctores, seu prædicatores, tenentur aliquo modo esse parati ad satisfactionem hujusmodi, quum apud Malachiam dicatur: Labia sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam, et legem requirent de ore ejus, quia angelus Domini exercituum est. In primitiva quoque Ecclesia, præparatio et eruditio ista ad satisfactionem talem magis necessaria fuit, quam nunc: quia tunc fideles inter perfidos undique morabantur, et sæpe inde interrogabantur, etiam a tyrannis. Fuitque eis necesse fidem contra adversarios ejus defendere.
paras.en: Nevertheless, to defend the faith against the disputing of adversaries, and to commend and set it forth reasonably by various arguments, is not for all, but especially for the learned. Nor is it a precept that every one of the faithful be ready to satisfy those who ask the reason of faith and hope, since many are unlettered and wholly simple; rather this is a counsel [that is, advice of perfection, not a binding command]. Prelates, however, and superiors and doctors or preachers are bound in some manner to be ready for such satisfaction, since it is said in Malachias: [[Mal 2:7|the lips of the priests shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth: because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts|Labia sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam, et legem requirent de ore ejus, quia angelus Domini exercituum est]]. In the primitive Church, too, this preparation and learning for such satisfaction was more necessary than now: because then the faithful dwelt everywhere among unbelievers, and were often questioned on this, even by tyrants; and it was necessary for them to defend the faith against its adversaries.

paras.t: Sed cum modestia et timore, id est, postulantibus a vobis rationem fidei vestræ ac spei, respondete modeste et timorate, humiliter et decenter, ne interrogatores scandalizentur in vobis, et se despici arbitrantes, contra fidem et ejus professores gravius accendantur. Hinc ad Romanos loquitur Paulus: Infirmum in fide assumite, non in disceptationibus cogitationum. Timotheo quoque scribens: Noli, inquit, verbis contendere: ad nihil enim utile est, nisi ad subversionem audientium. Itemque: Servum Domini non oportet litigare, sed patientem esse, et cum modestia corripientem eos qui resistunt. Denique, quum ea quæ fidei sunt, sint tam sublimia, incomprehensibilissima ac profunda, non nisi cum casto Dei timore de eis loqui et disputare debemus, ne forsitan Dominum offendamus, irreverenter et præsumptuose loquendo de ipso et mysteriis ejus: quia ut in Proverbiis asseritur, Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum, sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria. Propter quod, ut divinus Dionysius et Damascenus affirmant, non est audendum aliquid dicere de superessentiali Deitate, præter ea quæ nobis sunt in sacris eloquiis tradita. Conscientiam habentes bonam, ita ut vobis non sitis conscii de aliqua simulatione, nequitia aut culpa occulta, quemadmodum ad Corinthios asserit Paulus: Gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ, quod in simplicitate et sinceritate Dei, non in sapientia carnali, conversati sumus in hoc mundo.
paras.en: [[3:16|But with modesty and fear|Sed cum modestia et timore]], that is, to those who ask of you the reason of your faith and hope, answer modestly and with fear, humbly and becomingly, lest the questioners be scandalized in you and, thinking themselves despised, be more grievously inflamed against the faith and its professors. Hence Paul says to the Romans: [[Rom 14:1|him that is weak in faith, take unto you: not in disputes about thoughts|Infirmum in fide assumite, non in disceptationibus cogitationum]]. And writing to Timothy: [[2 Tim 2:14|Contend not in words: for it is to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers|Noli … verbis contendere … subversionem audientium]]. And again: [[2 Tim 2:24|the servant of the Lord must not wrangle|Servum Domini non oportet litigare]], but be patient, [[2 Tim 2:25|With modesty admonishing them that resist|cum modestia corripientem eos qui resistunt]]. Finally, since the things of faith are so sublime, so utterly incomprehensible and profound, we ought not to speak and dispute of them except with the chaste fear of God, lest perhaps we offend the Lord by speaking irreverently and presumptuously of him and his mysteries: for, as is said in Proverbs, [[Prov 25:27|As it is not good for a man to eat much honey, so he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory|Sicut qui mel comedit multum, non est ei bonum, sic qui perscrutator est majestatis, opprimetur a gloria]]. Wherefore, as the divine Dionysius and Damascene affirm, we must not dare to say anything of the superessential Deity beyond what is handed down to us in the sacred oracles. [[3:16|having a good conscience|Conscientiam habentes bonam]], so that you are not conscious to yourselves of any pretence, wickedness or hidden fault, as Paul asserts to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 1:12|our glory is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity of heart and sincerity of God, and not in carnal wisdom|Gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ, quod in simplicitate et sinceritate Dei, non in sapientia carnali]], we have conversed in this world.

paras.t: Ut in eo quod detrahunt de vobis, confundantur qui calumniantur vestram bonam conversationem, id est, detractores vestri, vobis incaute obloquentes, ex vestra rationabili responsione quam eis assignatis de fide et spe vestra, atque ex sancta vita vestra, confundantur, ipsa evidentia veritatis ac virtutis convicti, aut etiam tandem conversi. Vel, Confundantur in die judicii, quando justi stabunt in magna constantia adversus persecutores, irrisores, detractoresque suos. Unde per Jeremiam ait vir justus: Confundantur qui persequuntur me, et non confundar ego; paveant illi, et non paveam ego: induc super eos diem afflictionis. Hinc ad Titum habetur: Verbum sanum sit et irreprehensibile, ut is qui ex adverso est, vereatur, nihil mali habens loqui de vobis.
paras.en: [[3:16|that whereas they speak evil of you, they may be ashamed who falsely accuse your good conversation|Ut in eo quod detrahunt de vobis, confundantur qui calumniantur vestram bonam conversationem]], that is, your detractors, who rashly speak against you, may be confounded by the reasonable answer you give them about your faith and hope, and by your holy life, being convicted by the very evidence of truth and virtue, or even at length converted. Or: may be confounded at the day of judgment, when the just shall stand with great constancy against their persecutors, mockers and detractors[[Wis 5:1||]]. Hence through Jeremias the just man says: [[Jer 17:18|Let them be confounded that persecute me, and let not me be confounded: let them be afraid, and let not me be afraid: bring upon them the day of affliction|Confundantur qui persequuntur me, et non confundar ego; paveant illi, et non paveam ego: induc super eos diem afflictionis]]. Hence we have in the Epistle to Titus: [[Tit 2:8|The sound word that can not be blamed: that he who is on the contrary part may be afraid, having no evil to say|Verbum sanum sit et irreprehensibile, ut is qui ex adverso est, vereatur, nihil mali habens loqui]] of you.

paras.t: Hæc igitur agite cum bona conscientia, nec ex timore persecutionum omittite ea. Melius est enim, id est magis laudabile, magisque meritorium, benefacientes si velit voluntas Dei pati adversa, quam malefacientes: hoc est, virtuosius fuerit ut absque demerito vestro, utpote bene viventes, sustineatis adversa, quam ut ea pro vestris demeritis sustineatis, utpote male viventes: quemadmodum Job et Tobias amplius commendantur pro eo quod tanta perpessi sunt non pro suis excessibus, sed pro sua exercitatione et coronatione gloriosiori, atque ut aliis in exempla patientiæ ponerentur, quam Elymas magus et Joram, qui pro suis criminibus sunt plagati. Hac quoque auctoritate, secundum Bedam, reprehenditur eorum stultitia qui æquanimiter ferunt correptionem et correctionem quando culpabiles sunt, si vero absque culpa sua patiantur adversa aut arguantur, ægre accipiunt: et qui hactenus videbantur innoxii, per propriam iram, impatientiam, murmurationem, se noxios reddunt.
paras.en: Do these things, then, with a good conscience, and do not omit them for fear of persecutions. [[3:17|For it is better|Melius est enim]], that is, more praiseworthy and more meritorious, [[3:17|doing well (if such be the will of God) to suffer than doing ill|benefacientes si velit voluntas Dei pati adversa, quam malefacientes]] [Denis's text: “if the will of God will it, to suffer adversities”]: that is, it is more virtuous that you should endure adversities without demerit of your own, as living well, than that you should endure them for your demerits, as living ill: just as Job and Tobias are more commended because they suffered such things not for their own excesses, but for their exercise and more glorious crowning, and that they might be set as examples of patience to others[[Tob 2:12||]], than Elymas the magician[[Acts 13:8||]] and Joram[[2 Par 21:12||]], who were struck for their crimes. By this authority also, according to Bede, is rebuked the folly of those who bear reproof and correction with equanimity when they are guilty, but if they suffer adversity or are reproved without fault of their own, take it ill: and those who till then seemed harmless make themselves guilty by their own anger, impatience and murmuring.

paras.t: Porro, quod virtuosius sit absque proprio demerito pati, probat exemplo Christi. Quia et Christus semel pro peccatis nostris mortuus est: sicut ait in Psalmo, Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam. Et Jeremias in Threnis testatur: Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris. Mortuus ergo est pro peccatis nostris tollendis, sicut prædixit sanctissimus Joannes Baptista: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi. Crucifixus est enim ut merito suæ acerbissimæ passionis, in quantum illam ex ferventissima caritate atque plenissima obedientia acceptavit ac pertulit, pro nostris satisfaceret culpis, et copiosissimam nobis gratiam plenamque beatitudinem promereretur, juxta illud ad Hebræos: Sanguis Christi, qui semetipsum per Spiritum Sanctum obtulit immaculatum Deo, emundabit conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuis, ad serviendum Deo viventi: et rursus: Semel oblatus est, ad multorum exhaurienda peccata. Recteque additur, Semel, quia ut Paulus fatetur: Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur, mors illi ultra non dominabitur: quod enim mortuus est peccato, mortuus est semel. — Itaque, mortuus est pro nobis, justus pro injustis, videlicet ipse sanctus et innocens pro nobis transgressoribus, ut nos offerret Deo, id est, ei reconciliaret, et ad cœlestem introduceret patriam, quemadmodum ipse dixit, passione instante: Vado parare vobis locum, ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis. Christus quippe est qui fortem armatum, puta diabolum, ligavit, et spolia ejus distribuit, auferens ei quos ille deceperat, et ad Deum eos reducens: atque in altum ascendens, captivam duxit captivitatem. Propter quod per Isaiam Deus Pater ait de homine Christo: In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos, et iniquitates eorum ipse portabit: ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia. Etenim spolia fortium erant peccatores, a dæmonibus victi et capti: quorum multos, omnes scilicet electos, Christus sua passione, non solum sufficienter, sed et efficienter salvavit. Hinc scriptum est ad Ephesios: Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut exhiberet ipse sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam. — Offerret, inquam, nos Deo, mortificatos quidem carne, id est a carnalibus desideriis et inquinamentis abstractos, et spiritualiter mortuos, vivificatos autem spiritu, id est mente viventes in caritate et gratia; vel, Vivificatos spiritu, id est a Spiritu Sancto, per dona gratiæ ejus spiritualiter vivos effectos. Hanc enim mortificationem vivificam merito passionis Christi a Deo consequimur, nec sine ea finalem fructum dominicæ passionis, videlicet æternam salutem, adipiscemur. Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigunt, ut loquitur Paulus ad Galatas. Qui denuo ad Corinthios fatetur: Pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, ut qui vivunt, jam non sibi vivant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est et resurrexit.
paras.en: Further, that it is more virtuous to suffer without one's own demerit he proves by the example of Christ. [[3:18|Because Christ also died once for our sins|Quia et Christus semel pro peccatis nostris mortuus est]]: as he says in the Psalm, [[Ps 68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam]]. And Jeremias testifies in the Lamentations: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]]. He died, then, to take away our sins, as the most holy John the Baptist foretold: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi]]. For he was crucified that by the merit of his most bitter passion, inasmuch as he accepted and bore it out of most fervent charity and most complete obedience, he might satisfy for our faults and merit for us most abundant grace and full beatitude, according to that to the Hebrews: [[Heb 9:14|the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?|Sanguis Christi, qui semetipsum per Spiritum Sanctum obtulit immaculatum Deo, emundabit conscientiam nostram ab operibus mortuis, ad serviendum Deo viventi]]; and again: [[Heb 9:28|was offered once to exhaust the sins of many|Semel oblatus est, ad multorum exhaurienda peccata]]. And rightly is *once* added, because, as Paul declares: [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more. Death shall no more have dominion over him|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur, mors illi ultra non dominabitur]]: [[Rom 6:10|in that he died to sin, he died once|quod enim mortuus est peccato, mortuus est semel]]. — So he died for us, [[3:18|the just for the unjust|justus pro injustis]], namely he, holy and innocent, for us transgressors, [[3:18|that he might offer us to God|ut nos offerret Deo]], that is, reconcile us to him and bring us into the heavenly fatherland, as he himself said when his passion was at hand: [[John 14:2|I go to prepare a place for you|Vado parare vobis locum]], [[John 14:3|that where I am, you also may be|ut ubi sum ego, et vos sitis]]. For it is Christ who bound the strong man armed, that is, the devil, and distributed his spoils[[Matt 12:29||]][[Luke 11:21||]], taking from him those whom he had deceived and bringing them back to God; and ascending on high he led captivity captive[[Ps 67:19||]][[Eph 4:8||]]. Wherefore through Isaias God the Father says of the man Christ: [[Is 53:11|by his knowledge shall this my just servant justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities|In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos, et iniquitates eorum ipse portabit]]: [[Is 53:12|Therefore will I distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong|ideo dispertiam ei plurimos, et fortium dividet spolia]]. For the spoils of the strong were sinners, conquered and taken captive by demons: of whom Christ by his passion saved many, namely all the elect, not only sufficiently but also efficaciously [that is, his passion was enough for all, and actually brings salvation to the elect]. Hence it is written to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for it|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:27|That he might present it to himself, a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle|ut exhiberet ipse sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam]]. — He might offer us, I say, to God, [[3:18|being put to death indeed in the flesh|mortificatos quidem carne]] [Denis's text has the plural, referring to us], that is, withdrawn from carnal desires and defilements and spiritually dead, [[3:18|but enlivened in the spirit|vivificatos autem spiritu]], that is, living in mind in charity and grace; or, *enlivened in the spirit*, that is, made spiritually alive by the Holy Ghost through the gifts of his grace. For this life-giving mortification we obtain from God by the merit of Christ's passion, and without it we shall not attain the final fruit of the Lord's passion, namely eternal salvation. For [[Gal 5:24|they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigunt]], as Paul says to the Galatians. Who again declares to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 5:15|Christ died for all: that they also who live may not now live to themselves, but unto him who died for them and rose again|Pro omnibus mortuus est Christus, ut qui vivunt, jam non sibi vivant, sed ei qui pro ipsis mortuus est et resurrexit]].

paras.t: Itaque, qui tribulationes et persecutiones absque suis demeritis sibi illatas æquanimiter ferunt, Christo assimilantur. Qui vero eas pro suis peccatis tolerant patienter, conformantur latroni ad dexteram Christi suspenso, qui dixit, Digna factis recipimus; qui et cum Christo paradisum de cruce introivit. Qui vero nec pro suis excessibus corripi corrigique dignantur, latroni ad sinistram Salvatoris suspenso æquantur.
paras.en: So those who bear with equanimity tribulations and persecutions brought on them without their own demerits are made like to Christ. Those who endure them patiently for their sins are conformed to the thief hanged at the right hand of Christ, who said: [[Luke 23:41|we receive the due reward of our deeds|Digna factis recipimus]]; who also entered paradise from the cross with Christ. But those who do not deign to be reproved and corrected even for their own excesses are made equal to the thief hanged at the Saviour's left.

paras.t: Consequenter commemorat princeps Apostolorum antiquum opus misericordiæ Christi quod tempore Noe fecit: per quod præfiguravit effectum pietatis quem post suam incarnationem, in mundo hoc vivens, per se ipsum ac suos discipulos impendit hominibus. Est autem locus hic intricatus, et satis obscurus, ac variis modis translatus. Nam Beda ponit hunc textum: In quo et eis qui in carne conclusi erant, spiritu veniens, prædicavit. Quem textum sequitur et exponit Albertus. Alia vero translatio, teste Beda, sic habet: In quo spiritu et eis qui in carne erant, prædicavit, etc. Communiter vero ita habemus: In quo et his qui in carcere erant, spiritu veniens, vel, spiritualiter adveniens, prædicavit.
paras.en: Next the prince of the Apostles recalls an ancient work of Christ's mercy which he did in the time of Noe: by which he prefigured the effect of loving-kindness which after his incarnation, living in this world, he bestowed on men by himself and his disciples. Now this passage is intricate and rather obscure, and has been translated in various ways. For Bede gives this text: In which also coming in spirit he preached to those who were shut up in the flesh. This text Albert follows and expounds. Another translation, as Bede witnesses, has thus: In which spirit he preached also to those who were in the flesh, etc. But commonly we have thus: [[3:19|In which also coming he preached to those spirits that were in prison|In quo et his qui in carcere erant]], [[3:19|coming he preached|spiritu veniens, prædicavit]] [Denis reads “coming in spirit, or, coming spiritually, he preached”].

paras.t: Exponendo ergo hanc litteram, primo iste est sensus: In quo, id est ad hoc ut homines a se conversos Deo offerret; vel, In quo, id est in Spiritu Sancto, de quo (secundum unam expositionem) immediate præmisit, Vivificatos spiritu. Itaque, In quo et his qui in carcere erant, spiritu veniens, id est, Christus verus Deus per Spiritus Sancti immissionem seu inspirationem adveniens, his qui erant in carcere, id est, in profundo vitiorum et ignorantiarum, et consuetudine vitiosa erant ligati, propriisque iniquitatibus quasi custodia carcerali detenti, prout in Proverbiis habetur: Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur. Unde et Paulus loquens de impiis: Resipiscant (inquit) a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur. His ergo Christus per suæ miserationis effectum spiritualiter veniens, et Spiritu Sancto operante adveniens, prædicavit per Noe, ut infra innuitur: quem Noe Christus per inspirationem Spiritus Sancti instigavit ad prædicandum verbis et factis futurum esse diluvium propter scelera hominum, quia tunc omnis caro corruperat viam suam, ut dicitur in Genesi. Qui increduli fuerant aliquando, scilicet tempore Noe, cujus prædicationi non crediderunt, nec a suis cessaverunt criminibus, quando exspectabat Dei patientia, id est, Deus diu et patienter exspectavit pœnitentiam emendationemque hominum: quia per centum annos et amplius prænuntiavit diluvium esse futurum. Nam et Noe centum annis occupatus fuit cum suis in arcæ fabricatione, sicut ex Genesi trahitur. Hinc subditur: in diebus Noe quum fabricaretur arca, Deo dicente ad Noe: Fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigatis. Quidam textus habent, Quando exspectabant Dei patientiam: quia iniqui illi distulerunt et neglexerunt se emendare, videntes comminationem Dei de adventu diluvii tam diu differri. Sicque exspectabant patientiam Dei, non desiderando gratiam emendationis, sed diu manendo in suis peccatis, putantes quod pius et patiens Deus non esset eis diluvium inducturus. Sicque unicuique eorum dici poterat illud ad Romanos: Existimas quia tu effugies judicium Dei? An divitias bonitatis Dei et patientiæ et longanimitatis contemnis? Ignoras quoniam benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit? Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei.
paras.en: In expounding this text, then, the first sense is this: [[3:19|In which|In quo]], that is, to this end, that he might offer to God men converted by him; or, *in which*, that is, in the Holy Ghost, of whom (according to one exposition) he had just said, *enlivened in the spirit*. So: [[3:19|In which also coming he preached to those spirits that were in prison|In quo et his qui in carcere erant]], coming in spirit, that is, Christ, true God, coming by the sending or inspiration of the Holy Ghost to those who were in prison, that is, in the depth of vices and ignorances, who were bound by vicious habit and held by their own iniquities as in prison custody, as we have in Proverbs: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]]. Hence Paul too, speaking of the wicked, says: [[2 Tim 2:26|recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive|Resipiscant (inquit) a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur]]. To these, then, Christ, coming spiritually by the effect of his mercy, and arriving by the working of the Holy Ghost, [[3:19|preached|prædicavit]] through Noe, as is hinted below: which Noe Christ, by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, moved to preach by words and deeds that the flood was to come because of the crimes of men, for then [[Gen 6:12|all flesh had corrupted its way|omnis caro corruperat viam suam]], as is said in Genesis. [[3:20|Which had been some time incredulous|Qui increduli fuerant aliquando]], namely in the time of Noe, whose preaching they did not believe, nor did they cease from their crimes, [[3:20|when they waited for the patience of God|quando exspectabat Dei patientia]] [Denis's text reads “when the patience of God waited”], that is, God long and patiently awaited the repentance and amendment of men: for during a hundred years and more he foretold that the flood would come. For Noe too was occupied with his family for a hundred years in building the ark, as is gathered from Genesis[[Gen 5:31||]][[Gen 7:6||]]. Hence it is added: [[3:20|in the days of Noe, when the ark was a building|in diebus Noe quum fabricaretur arca]], God saying to Noe: [[Gen 6:14|Make thee an ark of timber planks|Fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigatis]]. Some texts have, *When they waited for the patience of God*: because those wicked men put off and neglected to amend themselves, seeing God's threat of the coming flood so long deferred. And so they waited for God's patience, not desiring the grace of amendment, but remaining long in their sins, thinking that the kind and patient God would not bring the flood upon them. And so to each of them could be said that word to the Romans: [[Rom 2:3|thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them who do such things and dost the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?|Existimas quia tu effugies judicium Dei?]]? [[Rom 2:4|despisest thou the riches of his goodness and patience and longsuffering? Knowest thou not that the benignity of God leadeth thee to penance?|An divitias bonitatis Dei et patientiæ et longanimitatis contemnis? Ignoras quoniam benignitas Dei ad pœnitentiam te adducit?]]? [[Rom 2:5|according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up to thyself wrath, against the day of wrath and revelation of the just judgment of God|Secundum duritiam autem tuam et impœnitens cor tuum, thesaurizas tibi iram in die iræ et revelationis justi judicii Dei]].

paras.t: Porro prætacta littera qua utitur Beda, sic intelligitur: Eis qui in carne erant conclusi, id est, carnalibus concupiscentiis devincti ac victi. Qui enim carnalibus magis quam Deo et spiritualibus rebus inhæret, recte in carne dicitur esse conclusus, quia non levat se supra se. De quibus ad Romanos asseritur: Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt. Virtuosis autem hominibus ibi mox additur: Vos in carne non estis, sed in spiritu. Cetera exponuntur ut habitum est.
paras.en: Further, the text mentioned above which Bede uses is understood thus: To those who were shut up in the flesh, that is, bound and overcome by carnal concupiscences. For he who cleaves to carnal things more than to God and spiritual things is rightly said to be shut up in the flesh, because he does not lift himself above himself. Of whom it is said to the Romans: [[Rom 8:8|they who are in the flesh cannot please God|Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt]]. But to virtuous men it is added there straightway: [[Rom 8:9|you are not in the flesh, but the spirit, if so be that the Spirit|Vos in carne non estis, sed in spiritu]]. The rest is expounded as has been said.

paras.t: Vult itaque princeps Apostolorum asserere quod Christus, qui nostris temporibus carne indutus, veniens prædicavit hominibus iter salutis, ipse etiam et ante diluvium eis qui tunc increduli erant, spiritu veniens prædicavit. Ipse namque per Spiritum Sanctum erat in Noe et in aliis Sanctis qui tunc erant, per quos tunc prædicavit iniquis illius temporis, ut converterentur. Sicque beatissimus Petrus in verbis istis apertissime innuit Christi divinitatem, et utriusque naturæ unam esse personam in ipso. Quamvis enim tunc nondum fuerit incarnatus, tamen vere tunc, imo et æternaliter fuit et est, quia suppositum est æternum. Et Christus supponit personam æternam et increatam. Propter quod ait in Joanne: Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum. Ad quod insinuandum, Judas apostolus in sua ait Canonica: Jesus populum salvans de terra Ægypti, secundo eos qui non crediderunt, perdidit. Ad Hebræos quoque fertur: Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula.
paras.en: So the prince of the Apostles means to assert that Christ, who in our times, clothed in flesh, came and preached to men the way of salvation, himself also before the flood, coming in spirit, preached to those who were then unbelieving. For he was through the Holy Ghost in Noe and in the other Saints who then lived, through whom he then preached to the wicked of that time, that they might be converted. And so the most blessed Peter in these words most plainly intimates the divinity of Christ, and that there is one person of both natures in him. For although he was not then yet incarnate, yet he truly was then, nay was and is eternally, because the suppositum is eternal [that is, the individual subject, the Person of the Word]. And *Christ* stands for an eternal and uncreated person. Wherefore he says in John: [[John 8:58|before Abraham was made, I AM|Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum]]. To intimate this, Jude the apostle says in his Canonical Epistle: [[Jude 1:5|Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not|Jesus populum salvans de terra Ægypti, secundo eos qui non crediderunt, perdidit]]. To the Hebrews also it is said: [[Heb 13:8|Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today: and the same for ever|Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula]].
