paras.t: Insuper quidam per carcerem intelligunt limbum patrum, ut sit sensus: In quo, ut scilicet plures Deo offerret ipse Christus, veniens spiritu, id est secundum animam suam, in carcerem, id est in limbum ubi sancti patres detinebantur (in quem Christus, ut spiritum tradidit, secundum animam mox descendit); prædicavit his qui detinebantur ibidem, id est, mysterium suæ incarnationis et passionis impletum esse annuntiavit: qui increduli fuerant aliquando, quando exspectabat Dei patientia in diebus Noe, quum fabricaretur arca, etc.: quia (ut pie speratur) quidam qui ante diluvium increduli erant verbis Noe, veniente ipso diluvio, suæ perfidiæ cognoverunt errorem, et pœnituerunt ac salvabantur, ita quod in purgatorio plene purgati, venerunt in limbum patrum, sicque eis cum ceteris ibi manentibus Christus, ut dictum est, prædicavit.
paras.en: Moreover, some understand by the prison the limbo of the fathers, so that the sense is: In which, namely that he might offer more to God, Christ himself, coming in spirit, that is, according to his soul, into the prison, that is, into limbo where the holy fathers were detained (into which Christ, as soon as he gave up the ghost, at once descended according to his soul), preached to those who were held there, that is, announced that the mystery of his incarnation and passion was fulfilled: [[3:20|Which had been some time incredulous, when they waited for the patience of God in the days of Noe, when the ark was a building|qui increduli fuerant aliquando, quando exspectabat Dei patientia in diebus Noe, quum fabricaretur arca]], etc.: because (as is piously hoped) some who before the flood were unbelieving at the words of Noe, when the flood itself came, recognized the error of their unbelief, and repented and were saved, so that, fully purged in purgatory, they came into the limbo of the fathers; and so to them, with the others remaining there, Christ preached, as has been said.

paras.t: — Quidam vero incaute, imo et insipienter dixerunt, quod Christus in infernum descendens, prædicavit ibi detentis pœnitentiam et viam salutis, seque mundi salvatorem consistere, et quod tunc credentes in eum salvabantur: inter quos quidam dixerunt Platonem fuisse primum credentium. Istud inter apocryphorum computandum est somnium. Et S. Cyrillus atque Chrysostomus huic contradicunt assertioni. Tempus quippe et status merendi ac demerendi, finem accipiunt in cujuslibet hominis morte. Propter quod asserit Damascenus: Quod angelis est ruina, hoc hominibus est mors. Et in Ecclesiaste legitur: Si ceciderit lignum ad austrum aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit. Idcirco de lege communi post vitam præsentem non est reditus ad pœnitentiam salutarem. Sed Deus omni lege sublimior est; et quibusdam, ut vult, privilegium facit.
paras.en: — But some have said incautiously, nay even foolishly, that Christ descending into hell preached to those held there repentance and the way of salvation, and that he was the Saviour of the world, and that those who then believed in him were saved: among whom some said that Plato was the first of the believers. This must be counted among the dreams of the apocrypha. And St. Cyril and Chrysostom contradict this assertion. For the time and state of meriting and demeriting come to an end at the death of every man. Wherefore Damascene asserts: What the fall is to the angels, that death is to men. And in Ecclesiastes we read: [[Eccles 11:3|If the tree fall to the south, or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be|Si ceciderit lignum ad austrum aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit]]. Therefore by the common law there is no return to saving repentance after the present life. But God is higher than every law, and grants a privilege to some as he wills.

paras.t: In qua arca pauci, id est octo animæ, sumendo partem pro toto, id est octo homines, utpote Noe et uxor ipsius, tres quoque filii Noe, et tres eorum uxores, salvæ factæ sunt, id est a periculo diluvii, scilicet submersione et morte, per aquam, id est per hoc quod aqua diluvii elevavit arcam in altum, ne mergerentur. Sumitur autem in Scripturis multoties pars pro toto: sicut in Psalmo, Ad te omnis caro veniet; et in Actibus, Eramus omnes animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex.
paras.en: [[3:20|wherein a few, that is, eight souls|In qua arca pauci, id est octo animæ]] — in which ark — taking the part for the whole, that is, eight persons, namely Noe and his wife, and the three sons of Noe and their three wives[[Gen 6:18||]][[Gen 7:7||]][[Gen 8:18||]], [[3:20|were saved|salvæ factæ sunt]], that is, from the peril of the flood, namely drowning and death, [[3:20|by water|per aquam]], that is, by this, that the water of the flood lifted the ark on high, so that they were not sunk. Now in the Scriptures the part is often taken for the whole: as in the Psalm, [[Ps 64:3|all flesh shall come to thee|Ad te omnis caro veniet]]; and in the Acts, [[Acts 27:37|we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls|Eramus omnes animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex]].

paras.t: (Quod et vos nunc similis formæ salvos facit Baptisma. Ordo verborum in constructione hic est: Quod (supple, dico quia) Baptisma similis formæ, id est sacramentum Baptismatis Christi existens similis formæ, id est comparis modi cum aquis diluvii. Nam, sicut per aquam diluvii salvi facti sunt valde pauci, comparatione eorum qui perierunt diluvio; ita electi qui per Baptismum salvantur, perpauci sunt, comparatione fidelium reproborum et aliorum incredulorum. Propterea ait Salvator: Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam; et rursus, Nolite (inquit) timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Rursus, sicut aqua diluvii elevando arcam, salvavit exsistentes in ea, sic aqua Baptismi salvat, levando ad cœlum. Itaque, Baptisma similis formæ salvos vos facit, id est, purgat a vitiis atque ad alia sacramenta deducit. Est enim primum inter sacramenta, et janua ad alia. Non carnis depositio sordium, id est, corporalium fœditatum seu immunditiarum depositio non vos salvat, sed spiritualis interiorque ablutio. Ideo subditur: sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum, id est interrogatio quæ fit a baptizando adulto: interrogatio, inquam, bonæ conscientiæ in Deum, id est inquisitio an habeat conscientiam bonam in Deo, ita ut non fictus accedat, sed catholice credens, et boni propositi. Hæc interrogatio salvat, id est, per eam fit baptizandi salvatio. Aliter enim non consequitur quis Baptismi effectum, si adultus exsistat. Tunc enim ab ipso fit interrogatio, personaliterque respondet. Si autem sit infans, patrinus respondet pro eo. Per resurrectionem Jesu Christi, id est, an habeat conscientiam bonam in Deo per resurrectionem Jesu Christi, id est per vivam et formatam fidem resurrectionis Jesu Christi, recte credendo in eum. Qui enim credit Christum resurrexisse a mortuis, alia ejus mysteria facilius credere potest. Sicque resurrectio Christi valde specialem habet difficultatem credendi. Ideo scriptum est in Actibus: Virtute magna reddebant Apostoli testimonium resurrectionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri.
paras.en: [[3:21|Whereunto baptism, being of the like form, now saveth you also|Quod et vos nunc similis formæ salvos facit Baptisma]]. The order of the words in construction is this: *Whereunto* (supply: I say because) *baptism of like form*, that is, the sacrament of Christ's Baptism, being of like form, that is, of a manner comparable with the waters of the flood. For as through the water of the flood very few were saved, in comparison with those who perished in the flood, so the elect who are saved through Baptism are very few in comparison with the reprobate among the faithful and the other unbelievers. Therefore the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life: and few there are that find it!|Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam]]; and again: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite … timere … dare vobis regnum]]. Again, as the water of the flood, by lifting the ark, saved those in it, so the water of Baptism saves by lifting to heaven. So baptism of like form *saveth you*, that is, cleanses from vices and leads to the other sacraments; for it is the first among the sacraments and the door to the others. [[3:21|not the putting away of the filth of the flesh|Non carnis depositio sordium]], that is, the putting away of bodily foulness or uncleanness does not save you, but a spiritual and inward washing. Therefore it is added: [[3:21|but, the examination of a good conscience towards God|sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum]], that is, the questioning made of the adult to be baptized: the questioning, I say, of a good conscience towards God, that is, the inquiry whether he has a good conscience in God, so that he comes not feignedly but believing as a Catholic and of good purpose. This questioning saves, that is, through it the salvation of the one baptized comes about. For otherwise one does not obtain the effect of Baptism if he be an adult. For then the questioning is made of him and he answers in person; but if he be an infant, the godfather answers for him. [[3:21|by the resurrection of Jesus Christ|Per resurrectionem Jesu Christi]], that is, whether he has a good conscience in God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, that is, through a living and formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity] in the resurrection of Jesus Christ, believing rightly in him. For he who believes that Christ rose from the dead can more easily believe his other mysteries. And thus the resurrection of Christ has a very special difficulty of belief. Therefore it is written in the Acts: [[Acts 4:33|with great power did the Apostles give testimony of the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord|Virtute magna reddebant Apostoli testimonium resurrectionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri]].

paras.t: Qui est ad dexteram Dei Patris: juxta illud Marci: Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei. Dicitur autem Christus ad Dei dexteram esse, dupliciter: primo, in quantum est Deus, sedet et regnat Deo Patri æqualis; sed in quantum homo, dicitur ad Patris dexteram residere, id est in potioribus ejus bonis consistere, quia præ universis electis fruitur Deitate sublimiter, et omni felicitate impletus est, quantum capere potest natura creata. Deglutiens mortem: quia in primis sua benedicta passione sibi ipsi plenam corporis immortalitatem promeruit, deinde genus humanum a morte culpæ redemit, imo et a morte æternæ damnationis salvavit. Plenam quoque animæ et corporis beatitudinem, quæ omnem mortalitatem excludit, promeruit nobis: quam virtute et merito Christi tandem sortientur electi, puta in die judicii, quando mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, et juxta quod loquitur Paulus, implebitur sermo qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoria. Hinc subditur: ut vitæ æternæ heredes efficeremur, id est, æternam salutem hereditate consequeremur. Unde per Osee prophetam ait Salvator: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne.
paras.en: [[3:22|Who is on the right hand of God|Qui est ad dexteram Dei]] the Father: according to that of Mark: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei]]. Now Christ is said to be at God's right hand in two ways: first, inasmuch as he is God, he sits and reigns equal to God the Father; but inasmuch as he is man, he is said to sit at the Father's right hand, that is, to abide in his greater goods, because above all the elect he enjoys the Deity sublimely, and is filled with all felicity, as far as created nature can receive. [[3:22|swallowing down death|Deglutiens mortem]]: because first by his blessed passion he merited for himself full immortality of body, then redeemed mankind from the death of guilt, nay saved it from the death of eternal damnation. He merited for us also the full beatitude of soul and body, which excludes all mortality: which by the power and merit of Christ the elect will at length obtain, namely at the day of judgment, when [[1 Cor 15:53|this mortal must put on immortality|mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem]], and, as Paul says, [[1 Cor 15:54|the saying that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory|implebitur sermo qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoria]]. Hence it is added: [[3:22|that we might be made heirs of life everlasting|ut vitæ æternæ heredes efficeremur]], that is, that we might obtain eternal salvation as an inheritance. Hence through Osee the prophet the Saviour says: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne]].

paras.t: Profectus in cœlum in die ascensionis. Per quod nobis dedit fiduciam præbuitque exemplum beatificæ ascensionis in cœlum cum corpore glorificato et anima, obtinendæ in die judicii, quando dicet: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum, etc. Subjectis sibi angelis, et potestatibus, et virtutibus: quia super omnium angelicorum ordinum dignitatem, hierarchiam et excellentiam, elevatus est Christus in ascensione, secundum naturam assumptam. Quocirca sciendum, quod eo ipso quo Christi humanitas, in incarnatione Verbi æterni, unita est Verbo hypostatica unione, videlicet ad personale et increatum esse Verbi assumpta in unitate personæ, prælata est omni creaturæ, et toto universo dignior sublimiorque effecta. Tamen in quantum mortalitati et passibilitati fuit subjecta, erat quodammodo angelis sanctis inferior. Sed quia ad immortalem vitam surrexit, et super omnes cœlos usque ad dexteram Patris ascendit, idcirco in ascensione dicuntur angeli et ceteri chori cœlestes, ei subjecti.
paras.en: [[3:22|being gone into heaven|Profectus in cœlum]] on the day of the ascension. By which he gave us confidence and offered an example of the beatifying ascension into heaven with glorified body and soul, to be obtained at the day of judgment, when he shall say: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum]], etc. [[3:22|the angels and powers and virtues being made subject to him|Subjectis sibi angelis, et potestatibus, et virtutibus]]: because above the dignity, hierarchy and excellence of all the angelic orders Christ was raised in the ascension, according to the nature assumed. Wherefore it must be known that by the very fact that Christ's humanity, in the incarnation of the eternal Word, was united to the Word by hypostatic union [that is, union in the one Person], namely assumed to the personal and uncreated being of the Word in unity of person, it was set above every creature and made worthier and more sublime than the whole universe. Yet inasmuch as it was subject to mortality and passibility, it was in a certain manner lower than the holy angels. But because he rose to immortal life and ascended above all the heavens even to the Father's right hand, therefore in the ascension the angels and the other heavenly choirs are said to be subject to him.

paras.t: Et exprimuntur hic tres chori angelici, seu tres ordines angelorum, per quos ceteri dantur intelligi. Quocirca pensandum, quod gloriosissimus apostolici agminis vertex, paulatim ascendendo, primo exprimit Angelos, deinde Potestates, et tertio loco Virtutes. Ex quo sumitur argumentum, quod Virtutes pertineant ad secundam hierarchiam angelicam, et supra Potestates exsistant, prout divinus Dionysius a Paulo apostolo informatus, edocuit: quamquam Gregorius et Bernardus ponant Virtutes in infima hierarchia chorum supremum.
paras.en: And three angelic choirs, or three orders of angels, are named here, by which the others are given to be understood. Wherefore it is to be weighed that the most glorious head of the apostolic band, ascending step by step, names first the Angels, then the Powers, and in the third place the Virtues. From which an argument is drawn that the Virtues belong to the second angelic hierarchy and stand above the Powers, as the divine Dionysius, instructed by the apostle Paul, taught: although Gregory and Bernard place the Virtues as the highest choir in the lowest hierarchy.
